subject: Request: Vulnerability remediation evidence and auditor-ready attestation
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@hightower.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Vulnerability remediation evidence for SIG / SOC 2 audit

Hi Laura,

We’re starting SIG and SOC 2 evidence collection for our scheduled audit next quarter. Auditor asks for proof of your vulnerability management program focused on: scan cadence, typical CVE remediation windows by severity, escalation path for critical findings, and a signed attestation we can include in the binder.

Can you provide:
- a short summary of scan cadence (internal + third‑party) and expected detection->fix timelines by CVE severity,
- a sample scan export (redacted) showing recent closure times,
- an auditor‑ready attestation we can rely on for the SIG/SOC 2 questionnaire?

We only need high level artifacts: a one‑page statement we can include in the binder and a CSV sample of a recent scan run. Also please confirm a single point of contact (email) for our auditor to reach out to for follow‑ups.

Thanks — appreciate a response this week if possible.

Best,
Anita Shah
Security Assurance Lead | Hightower Financial
anita.shah@hightower.com
+1 415‑555‑0132
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@hightower.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Vulnerability remediation evidence for SIG / SOC 2 audit

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary below and I’ve attached the materials you requested (sample scan export + our VM playbook + SLA spreadsheet).

Snapshot:
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated internal scans (codebase + infra), daily lightweight external scans for public endpoints, and monthly third‑party full stack scans. We also run targeted ad‑hoc scans for high‑risk deploys.
- Remediation windows (median observed): Critical: 72 hours (SLO 48–72h), High: 14 days (SLO 7–21d), Medium: 30 days, Low: next regular release. These are summarized in the attached SLO/SLA spreadsheet.
- Escalation path: Critical findings auto‑page oncall engineering + security, SOC2 runbook triggers a hotfix workflow; contact list and pager escalation are in the playbook.
- Evidence: attached CSV shows a recent run with CVE IDs, discovery timestamp, owner, patch status and close timestamp (redacted where required).

We can provide a signed one‑page attestation. I’ll coordinate with Kimberly (security operations) to sign and route that back to you via DocuSign by Friday. If auditors need an API key for automated evidence pulls we can provide scoped access for read‑only scan exports.

Point of contact for audit follow‑ups: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com (Security Ops Manager).

Attachments: redwood_vm_playbook.pdf, sample-scan-log-202510.csv, slo-and-sla-breakdown.xlsx

If you want any timing tighter than the windows above (for example firm 48‑hour critical fix guarantees), let me know and we can discuss a narrow SLA amendment.

Cheers,

Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Security Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
(650) 555‑0199
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@hightower.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: audit@hightower.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Vulnerability remediation evidence for SIG / SOC 2 audit

Laura — thanks, that looks helpful. A couple of clarifying requests from the audit team:

1) The auditor wants the attestation to explicitly state the CVE closure commitment windows we described (Critical/High/Medium) and to be signed by a security leader.
2) For critical CVEs they ask for a short description of the verification steps you use to confirm mitigation (e.g., verification scan, exploit test, or backport confirmation).
3) They prefer DocuSign for the signed statement; can you provide a link once ready?

Also — can Kimberly be the named contact for any technical follow‑ups (we’ll share the auditor’s calendar link before next Wednesday)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Hi Anita — attaching the signed attestation and a short verification note for critical CVEs. Kimberly reviewed and approved the language below; we routed the attestation through DocuSign so the binder will show a timestamped signature.

Attestation (summary):
Redwood Inference maintains a risk‑based vulnerability management program. We run weekly authenticated internal scans, daily external scans of production endpoints, and monthly full third‑party scans. Our operational SLOs for remediation are: Critical — 48–72 hours (median closure 72h), High — 7–21 days, Medium — 30 days, Low — included in next scheduled release. Critical findings trigger oncall escalation and verification that mitigation is effective via follow‑up verification scans and targeted validation tests; remediation is considered complete once verification scans confirm the CVE no longer appears in the vulnerable state or when a vendor patch is successfully backported and verified.

Signed by: Kimberly Park, Security Ops Manager — Redwood Inference
DocuSign record: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF123456

Attachments: signed-vm-attestation.pdf (DocuSigned), sample-scan-log-202510.csv, redwood_vm_playbook.pdf, slo-and-sla-breakdown.xlsx

If auditors want a short (15‑minute) technical review call with Kimberly next week, she’s available Tue/Thu mornings — I copied her here and she’ll confirm availability.

Thanks — let me know if you need anything else.

—Laura
